public_rationale: Marcus said object-permanence-type problems persisted across video models, including the Sora released the week of the post. TechCrunch's report on the first hands-on review of the December 9, 2024 Sora said it had object-permanence issues, with objects disappearing and reappearing for no reason, 'the same flaws as other generative tools.' OpenAI's launch post said the deployed Sora 'often generates unrealistic physics.' A 2024 benchmark (VideoPhy) found leading video models severely lacked physical commonsense. On a plain reading, which covers the leading models rather than literally every model, the claim holds.
limitations: 'All models' cannot be literally verified. The evidence covers the leading publicly evaluated models.
VideoPhy measures physics broadly, not object permanence specifically.
The Sora review is one reviewer's hands-on testing, as reported by TechCrunch.

our_interpretation: Plain reading: from February 2024 to the post date, leading AI video generators, including the Sora version released December 9, 2024, still showed object-permanence and similar physical-consistency failures, such as objects vanishing or reappearing.
'All models' is read as the leading publicly evaluated video models. Every model ever released is not checkable.
criteria.support_condition: Reviews or evaluations of the December 2024 Sora release showing object-permanence failures, plus evidence that other leading video models still had similar physics or consistency failures in 2024.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Credible evaluations showing the December 2024 Sora, or leading video models in general, had largely solved object permanence by the post date.

evidence.excerpt: it suffers from the same flaws as other generative tools out there, namely issues related to object permanence. In Sora videos, objects pass in front of each other or behind each other in ways that don’t make sense, and disappear and reappear without any reason.
evidence.explanation: The first review of the December 2024 Sora release found object-permanence failures and called them the same flaws as other generative tools. This matches both the Sora part and the 'all models' part.

evidence.excerpt: The version of Sora we are deploying has many limitations. It often generates unrealistic physics and struggles with complex actions over long durations.
evidence.explanation: OpenAI itself said the released Sora often generates unrealistic physics. This is consistent with continued physical-consistency problems.

evidence.excerpt: Our human evaluation reveals that the existing models severely lack the ability to generate videos adhering to the given text prompts, while also lack physical commonsense.
evidence.explanation: A 2024 benchmark of several open and closed video models found that even the best one followed physical laws in under 40% of cases. This supports the claim that such problems were widespread, though it measures physical commonsense broadly, not object permanence alone.
